stories.title: Northmarq Arranges Refi for Van Nuys Warehouse Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s Los Angeles Debt + Equity team, led by Zalmi Klyne and Stanley Chu, successfully arranged $6.1 million in permanent financing for three flex/showroom industrial properties located within the Los Angeles metro. Northmarq arranged financing on behalf of the borrower through a correspondent relationship with a life insurance company. The transaction was structured on a ten-year term. The portfolio included: 14943 Califa St. is a single-tenant industrial flex/showroom property built in 1955 and situated on a 0.33-acre site. The asset features a one-story design supporting a range of showroom, warehouse and light manufacturing uses. 15044 Keswick St. is a single-tenant industrial flex/showroom property built in 1969 and situated on a 1.48-acre site. 14932 Oxnard St. is a single-tenant industrial property situated on approximately 0.65 acres. Collectively, the three properties benefit from their locations in Van Nuys within the San Fernando Valley, one of Southern California’s most established infill industrial markets. The post Northmarq Arranges Refi for Van Nuys Warehouse Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Northmarq arranged $6.1M permanent financing for three Van Nuys industrial flex properties.
10-year term through life insurance correspondent; portfolio refinance on 1955–1969 assets.
Van Nuys San Fernando Valley established infill industrial market benefits from location.
stories.summary: Northmarq's LA debt team closed $6.1 million in permanent financing on a three-property industrial flex/showroom portfolio in Van Nuys, ranging from 0.33 to 1.48 acres and built between 1955 and 1969. The 10-year fixed loan was arranged through a life insurance company correspondent. The deal signals continued investor confidence in infill industrial real estate in Southern California's San Fernando Valley submarket.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. However, strong demand for industrial-flex refinancing at scale (even at $6.1M) in Van Nuys suggests tight cap rates and low distress in LA industrial, which may signal overall market health and investor appetite in the region that could support mixed-use or nearby residential development.

stories.title: Westfield Montgomery Owner Pays Off $350M Loan on Bethesda, Md., Mall
stories.excerpt: Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield (URW) has paid off a $350 million loan tied to the Westfield Montgomery shopping mall in Bethesda, Md., more than two years after the debt was transferred to special servicing. The 1.2 million-square-foot mall’s loan had been scheduled to mature Aug. 1, Bisnow reported. Morningstar Credit described the payoff as a “rarity in a cycle” in which many mall loans continue to receive extensions. URW secured the 10-year loan in 2014, with the debt tied to 836,000 square feet of the property. The mall received a two-year extension after missing its original August 2024 maturity date. French mall giant URW won approval in 2020 to redevelop Westfield Montgomery, but that project has not started. URW did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The payoff comes as URW has reversed course on its broader U.S. strategy. In 2022, the company said it planned to sell its $13.2 billion American portfolio, but last year opted instead to retain 11 high-performing flagship malls while continuing to unload non-core properties. Meanwhile, Westfield Montgomery has continued adding retailers and restaurants. The mall said in July that new arrivals throughout 2026 would include Pop Mart and Wetzel’s Pretzels, among others. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield (URW) paid off $350M Westfield Montgomery mall loan early.
Bethesda, Md. 1.2M-SF property exited special servicing after two-year extension.
URW retaining 11 flagship malls, reversing 2022 plan to sell $13.2B U.S. portfolio.
stories.summary: URW successfully paid off a $350 million loan on the 1.2-million-square-foot Westfield Montgomery mall in Bethesda, Md., exiting special servicing more than two years after the debt was transferred. The loan had been extended two years past its August 2024 maturity. URW has pivoted from its 2022 plan to sell its entire $13.2 billion U.S. portfolio, instead retaining 11 high-performing flagship properties while divesting non-core assets.
stories.impact: Minimal impact to multifamily development. The payoff signals URW's selective focus on flagship malls and reduced distress in trophy retail properties, but the company's delayed redevelopment plans (approved 2020, not yet started) and overall portfolio retrenchment underscore persistent mall sector challenges—relevant only if multifamily developers are competing for mixed-use urban sites in secondary markets like Bethesda.

stories.title: Childcare Franchise Adding 60K-SF of New Sacramento Locations
stories.excerpt: National daycare franchise The Learning Experience is expanding across Sacramento with six new locations opening over the next two years, adding 60,000 square feet of freestanding commercial real estate across the region. The Learning Experience locations each consist of up to 10,000 square feet of indoor building space with up to a 5,000-square-foot playground. Each new center will also employ as many as 30 staff members and certified teachers to serve upwards of 180 children between 6 weeks and 6 years of age with daycare and early childhood education. The Learning Experience, which currently has one location open and operating in the Sacramento market, plans to open six new locations in: Folsom – Q3 2027 Rocklin – Q3 2027 Dixon – Q4 2027 Turlock – Q1 2028 Lincoln – Q1 2028 Roseville – Q2 2029 The Florida-based franchise, which is owned by the private equity group Harvest Partners, now has 491 centers open and operating, including 488 in the U.S. and three in the U.K. The post Childcare Franchise Adding 60K-SF of New Sacramento Locations appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Learning Experience opening six 10K-SF freestanding daycare centers in Sacramento region Q3 2027–Q2 2029.
60K SF total commercial real estate across Folsom, Rocklin, Dixon, Turlock, Lincoln, Roseville.
Each location will employ ~30 staff, serve 180 children 6 weeks–6 years.
stories.summary: National daycare franchise The Learning Experience (owned by Harvest Partners PE) plans to open six new locations across the Sacramento metropolitan area over the next two years, adding 60,000 square feet of freestanding commercial space. Each center will occupy up to 10,000 square feet with a 5,000-SF playground and serve approximately 180 children per location with 30 staff members. The rollout spans Folsom, Rocklin, Dixon, Turlock, Lincoln, and Roseville between Q3 2027 and Q2 2029.
stories.impact: Signals strong demographic tailwinds and household formation in the greater Sacramento region. Childcare expansion typically lags population growth and young-family migration; this 60K-SF childcare commitment suggests confidence in sustained in-migration and family household growth across suburban Sacramento submarkets. Multifamily developers should anticipate elevated renters-with-children demand and family-oriented amenity expectations in these same corridors over the 2027–2029 delivery window.

stories.title: Vestal Point Capital Takes 12K SF at Rockrose Development’s 11 East 26th Street
stories.excerpt: Investment firm and hedge fund manager Vestal Point Capital is relocating its offices within New York City. The company has inked a long-term, 12,139-square-foot lease on the entire 12th floor of Rockrose Development’s 11 East 26th Street across the street from Manhattan’s Madison Square Park, Commercial Observer has learned. The company’s current address is listed on its website as 632 Broadway in NoHo. It is unclear when the firm will move. The exact length of the lease was unclear. The asking rent was more than $130 per square foot, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. Newmark‘s William Cohen and Ariel Harwood are the exclusive leasing agents for the property. Brian Goldman and Cooper Weisman — also from Newmark — represented the tenant in this deal. Newmark declined to comment, while a spokesperson for Vestal Point Capital did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Standing 21 stories tall, 11 East 26th Street is a two-building office complex connected to 15 East 26th Street. The second floor is a full-scale amenity club featuring a workout space, a private lounge, a designated area for whiskey lockers, and a grab-and-go kitchen. There is also a landscaped rooftop that includes terraces, seating areas, and an indoor-outdoor conference and entertainment space. Other tenants at 11 East 26th Street include artificial intelligence firm Sierra and business consulting firm Activate Consulting. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Vestal Point Capital leased 12,139 SF (entire 12th floor) at Rockrose's 11 East 26th Street, Manhattan.
Long-term lease at $130+ per SF asking; relocation from 632 Broadway NoHo.
Rockrose property is 21-story office complex adjacent to Madison Square Park.
stories.summary: Investment firm and hedge fund Vestal Point Capital has signed a long-term lease for 12,139 square feet (the entire 12th floor) at Rockrose Development's 11 East 26th Street in Flatiron/Madison Square Park, Manhattan, at asking rents exceeding $130 per square foot. The company is relocating from its NoHo headquarters at 632 Broadway. Newmark brokered the transaction on behalf of the tenant and the landlord.
stories.impact: Modest relevance to multifamily. The deal demonstrates robust office leasing demand and rent resilience in prime Manhattan submarkets (Flatiron); however, it also signals a financial services tenant's willingness to pay premium rates for trophy office space, which reflects capital and employment stability in NYC that supports broader residential demand. The move from NoHo to Flatiron may indicate neighborhood preference shifts that could influence multifamily site selection and positioning in Manhattan.

stories.title: NYC Human Resources Administration Extends 174K-SF Lease in Midtown
stories.excerpt: The New York City Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) extended the lease for a government agency in Midtown South. The New York City Human Resources Administration (HRA) will get an extra 18 months at Vornado Realty Trust’s 260 11th Avenue, where it occupies 174,186 square feet, according to a source close to the deal. The deal appeared in a monthly Manhattan office market report by Colliers, which offered no further insight into the deal apart from the average office asking rent for Midtown South, which was $78.90 in August. DCAS negotiated the deal on behalf of HRA, but it’s unclear who brokered the deal for Vornado, which declined to comment. HRA’s lease was scheduled to turn over in October, The Real Deal reported in September 2022, and at some point it may have expanded its footprint from its initial 154,000 square feet. The agency has locations throughout the city, including a 350,000-square-foot office at Clipper Equities‘ 250 Livingston Street, where it offers legal services, and a 9,199-square-foot post at 25 Chapel Street in Downtown Brooklyn, where it provides assistance to veterans. Located between West 26th and West 27th streets several blocks south of Hudson Yards, 260 11th Avenue is a seven-story landmarked building constructed in 1911 and is known as the Otis Elevator Building. Vornado holds a 99-year ground lease for the property. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: NYC Human Resources Administration extended 174K-SF lease at Vornado's 260 11th Avenue (Midtown South).
18-month extension; no new space added; average asking rent $78.90/SF in Midtown South.
HRA occupancy in Midtown South remains stable; government tenant retention.
stories.summary: The New York City Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) negotiated an 18-month lease extension for the Human Resources Administration at Vornado Realty Trust's 260 11th Avenue in Midtown South, covering 174,186 square feet. The extension replaced an October 2024 scheduled turnover. Average office asking rents in Midtown South stood at $78.90 per square foot at the time of the deal.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily. Government office lease extensions signal public-sector employment stability in Manhattan, which supports overall metro demand for rental housing. The Midtown South office market resilience (at $78.90/SF) suggests economic health and continued job density that underpin renter demand across Manhattan and nearby boroughs, benefiting multifamily development broadly.

stories.title: NAI Inks Leasing Deal for Two Long Beach Retail Centers
stories.excerpt: NAI Capital Commercial has been awarded the leasing assignment for two newly renovated, adjacent retail centers along Anaheim Street in Long Beach, California. David Maling will have the exclusive assignment. Located at 1320 Atlantic Avenue and 955 E Anaheim Street, at the northeast corners of Anaheim Street and Atlantic Avenue, and Anaheim Street and Lime Avenue, respectively, both centers have undergone extensive renovation and are anchored by Smart & Final and Aldi. Combined, the properties offer more than 140,000 square feet of retail space, with available suites ranging from approximately 1,079 to 6,174 square feet, outdoor patio and dining areas, ample parking, and strong traffic counts exceeding 50,000 and 35,000 vehicles per day at their respective intersections. Long Beach’s strong residential base, diverse employment centers, two major colleges and year-round coastal climate support consistent customer traffic. Nearby Downtown offers a vibrant mix of retail, dining and entertainment. The post NAI Inks Leasing Deal for Two Long Beach Retail Centers appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: NAI Capital awarded leasing for two adjacent Long Beach retail centers on Anaheim Street.
140K SF combined space, anchored by Smart & Final and Aldi; 1,079–6,174 SF suites.
Strong traffic: 50K and 35K daily vehicles; year-round coastal climate supports demand.
stories.summary: NAI Capital Commercial has been awarded the exclusive leasing assignment for two newly renovated adjacent retail centers at 1320 Atlantic Avenue and 955 E. Anaheim Street in Long Beach, California, featuring over 140,000 square feet combined. Both centers are anchored by Smart & Final and Aldi, with available suites ranging from 1,079 to 6,174 square feet. The properties sit at high-traffic intersections (50,000 and 35,000 daily vehicles) and benefit from Long Beach's diverse residential base, employment centers, two major colleges, and year-round coastal climate.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily impact. However, the strong retail momentum and traffic fundamentals (50K+ vehicles daily) in Long Beach indicate robust consumer spending and population density. Mixed-use or adjacent multifamily development near these anchored retail centers could benefit from co-tenancy and foot traffic; the continued capital commitment to retail renovation signals landlord confidence in Long Beach's demographic and economic resilience.

stories.title: Gantry Secures $23M for KS Multifamily Near Pittsburg State University
stories.excerpt: Gantry has secured a $22.75 million permanent loan for the University Digs apartment community located at 1902 S Broadway St in Pittsburg, Kansas, directly adjacent to Pittsburg State University. The three-story, 190-unit property features a mix of studio, one- and two-bedroom floorplans. Originally built in 1960, University Digs has undergone extensive renovations since then. Gantry’s Mark Reichter, Principal, and Alec Frook, Associate, with the firm’s Kansas City production office, represented the borrower, a private real estate investor. The five-year, non-recourse, fixed-rate loan was secured from one of Gantry’s preferred CMBS lenders and features full-term interest only. “University Digs is a well-located, stabilized asset with active management that performs in both a traditional multifamily and student housing model due to its proximity to Pittsburg State University, Mercy Hospital, and the restaurant, retail and cultural amenities of downtown Pittsburg,” said Reichter. bullets: Gantry secured $22.75M permanent CMBS loan for 190-unit University Digs in Pittsburg, Kansas.

Stabilized 1960 property renovated; serves dual student-housing and traditional multifamily model.
stories.summary: Gantry Capital arranged a $22.75 million permanent CMBS loan for University Digs, a 190-unit apartment community in Pittsburg, Kansas, directly adjacent to Pittsburg State University. The five-year, non-recourse, fixed-rate loan features interest-only payments and was sourced from a Gantry preferred CMBS lender. The property, originally built in 1960, has been extensively renovated and operates as a hybrid student-housing and traditional multifamily asset, also benefiting from proximity to Mercy Hospital and downtown Pittsburg amenities.
stories.impact: Demonstrates continued CMBS lending appetite for stabilized student-housing-adjacent multifamily in secondary markets. The successful permanent placement of a 190-unit renovation near a state university signals lender confidence in the dual student/traditional resident demand model and suggests opportunities for developers to acquire and reposition Class C student-adjacent assets in college towns with stable enrollment and regional employers (e.g., Mercy Hospital). Pittsburg's market stability enables long-term hold financing.

stories.title: Affinius Capital Lends $310M for Jersey City Multifamily Tower Build
stories.excerpt: The demand for apartments across the Hudson River keeps rising. Namdar Group has landed $310 million of construction financing to build a 47-story multifamily tower in Jersey City, N.J., Commercial Observer has learned. Affinius Capital originated the loan for Namdar’s 1,049-unit Park Tower project in Jersey City’s Journal Square neighborhood. The large-scale development was given the green light by the Jersey City Planning Board in June a year after it secured a $32 million pre-development loan from Post Road Group paving the way for the tower, Jersey Digs previously reported. “Park Tower will be among Journal Square’s premier multifamily projects capitalizing on the neighborhood’s continued growth,” David Greenburg, co-head of debt origination at Affinius, said in a statement. “This project aligns with our strategy of financing exceptional multifamily assets with top-tier sponsorship.” Walker & Dunlop negotiated the debt with a capital markets institutional advisory team consisting of Aaron Appel, Keith Kurland, Jonathan Schwartz, Adam Schwartz, Dustin Stolly, Sean Reimer, Jordan Casella, Christopher de Raet and Edward Leboyer. Located at 8-16 Lott Street, the Park Tower project will have a mix of floor plans ranging from studios to three-bedroom units. Community amenities will include a fitness center, a yoga studio, a bowling alley, an arcade, a music room, a golf simulator and a rooftop lounge. Long Island-based Namdar Group has been an active developer in Jersey City, recently completing a 27-story, 564-unit luxury apartment tower at 35 Cottage Street in Journal Square. It also inked a $335 million debt package to refinance three newly built Jersey City multifamily properties totaling 833 units at 9 Homestead Place, 26 Van Reipen Avenue and 28 Cottage Street, as CO previously first reported. Namdar Group did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Affinius Capital provided $310M construction financing for 1,049-unit Park Tower in Jersey City.
47-story tower at 8-16 Lott Street, Journal Square; Jersey City Planning Board approved June.
Loan follows $32M pre-development financing from Post Road Group; strong sponsor-driven multifamily pipeline.
stories.summary: Namdar Group has secured $310 million in construction financing from Affinius Capital for Park Tower, a 47-story, 1,049-unit multifamily tower in Jersey City's Journal Square neighborhood. The Jersey City Planning Board approved the large-scale project in June, following a $32 million pre-development loan from Post Road Group. Affinius highlighted the project's alignment with Journal Square's neighborhood growth and the developer's top-tier sponsorship as key drivers of the financing.
stories.impact: Strong signal of robust construction lending availability and investor appetite for large-scale multifamily development in Jersey City's Journal Square, a submarket experiencing significant transit-oriented growth and population in-migration from Manhattan. The $310M construction facility and prior pre-dev financing indicate capital markets confidence in Hudson-facing submarkets. Developers should view this as validation of Journal Square's demand fundamentals and a window to move forward on pipeline projects in Jersey City before the Journal Square submarket approaches saturation with Park Tower and competing deliveries.

stories.title: Go Outdoors Heads to Boston for Marina Purchase
stories.excerpt: Investment platform Go Outdoors has acquired Boston’s Constitution Marina for an undisclosed price, allowing the longtime owners of the top-rated waterfront facility to sail into retirement. Colliers brokered the sale of the 273-slip marina, representing the seller, Bosport Docking, LLC. Go Outdoors was not represented by a broker. Located at 28 Constitution Rd, the marina sits along Boston Harbor and the historic Freedom Trail in the Charlestown neighborhood, just outside downtown Boston. Constitutional Marina features roughly 9,000 linear feet of dockage along with protected transient and seasonal dockage and is rated among the top 3% of marinas nationwide on Marinas.com. The family that has owned and operated the marina for more than 60 years sought a buyer that would be a responsible and capable steward of the asset. Go Outdoors emerged as the new owner through a competitive call-for-offers process that led to 10 offers from qualified buyers, according to a statement by Colliers. Historically focused on the Southeast U.S., Go Outdoors owns 16 marinas and four RV resort parks along with its partner, Monarch Alternative Capital LP. The post Go Outdoors Heads to Boston for Marina Purchase appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Go Outdoors acquired Boston's Constitution Marina (273 slips) in Charlestown for undisclosed price.
9K linear feet dockage; top 3% rated marina nationwide; historic Freedom Trail location.

stories.summary: Go Outdoors has acquired Constitution Marina in Boston's Charlestown neighborhood for an undisclosed price through a competitive bidding process (10 offers). The 273-slip marina features roughly 9,000 linear feet of protected dockage and is rated among the top 3% of marinas nationwide on Marinas.com. Located on the historic Freedom Trail, the marina was operated by the same family for over 60 years. Go Outdoors, historically focused on the Southeast, now operates 16 marinas and four RV parks with partner Monarch Alternative Capital.
stories.impact: No direct relevance to multifamily development. Marina acquisitions do not drive multifamily demand, supply, or capital flows in residential markets.

stories.title: Industrious Adds 19th L.A.-Area Location at Caruso’s Masonic Temple
stories.excerpt: Coworking giant Industrious is adding another location in Southern California, this time at one of the more recognizable office properties in Glendale. The flexible office provider has signed for 12,000 square feet across two floors at Caruso’s historic Masonic Temple at 234 South Brand Boulevard, Commercial Observer can first report. The location is expected to open in late June 2027 as Industrious’ second in Glendale and 19th across Greater Los Angeles. It’s also Industrious’ first deal with Caruso. The new workspace will include 101 private office seats and 17 common-area seats. “Glendale has proven itself as a strong market for us, and we’re excited to build on that success with this new location,” Natalie Levine, director of real estate at Industrious, said in a statement. The nine-story Art Deco Masonic Temple was built in 1929, and Rick Caruso’s eponymous real estate company restored it as Class A office and retail space adjacent to the owner’s Americana at Brand shopping center. CBRE, which acquired Industrious last year, uses the property as its North L.A. headquarters. “Adding a premier flexible workplace within the historic Masonic Temple further strengthens the Americana at Brand’s live-work-play ecosystem, creating a seamless experience across one highly connected and walkable destination,” said Jackie Levy, chief revenue officer at Caruso. Industrious has been growing around Greater L.A. Earlier this year, the company opened an 18,400-square-foot location at Douglas Emmett’s Studio Plaza in Burbank, and signed a 22,000-square-foot deal at Sherman Oaks Galleria. The company also expanded aggressively across the Westside in recent years, including a 16,000-square-foot Beverly Hills location, roughly 44,000 square feet combined in Westwood and Santa Monica, and 19,000 square feet at Watt Plaza in Century City. Industrious operates more than 250 locations across more than 80 cities globally. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver
bullets: Industrious signed 12K SF (two floors) at Caruso's Masonic Temple, Glendale, California.
Opening late June 2027; 19th LA-area location, second in Glendale; 101 private offices.
9-story 1929 Art Deco landmark restored by Caruso to Class A office/retail.
stories.summary: Coworking provider Industrious has leased 12,000 square feet across two floors at Caruso's historic Masonic Temple at 234 South Brand Boulevard in Glendale, California, marking the company's 19th location in Greater Los Angeles and second in Glendale. The space will open in late June 2027 and will include 101 private office seats and 17 common-area seats. The 1929 Art Deco Masonic Temple was restored by Caruso as Class A office and retail, and this is Industrious' first deal with the Caruso portfolio.
stories.impact: Modest signal of office/flex-workspace demand recovery in Glendale and continued mixed-use activation of historic office properties in LA's secondary markets. Industrious' expansion to a 19th LA location suggests sustained demand for flexible office from small to mid-market tenants. For multifamily developers, the coworking expansion in Glendale complements broader LA demand and may justify Class A residential development near transit or established office clusters; however, coworking typically absorbs some marginal demand that might otherwise flow to apartments, warranting careful market segmentation in site selection.
